subject: Control ownership & evidence ramp-check for ISO27001 + FedRAMP readiness
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@brightline.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: security@brightline.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Initial ask: roadmap, control owners & evidence windows for ISO/FedRAMP readiness

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As Brightline prepares its vendor assessment, we need a concise view into Redwood's near-term certification roadmap so our audit team can plan dependencies. Specifically, could you please confirm the following by EOD Friday: 

- High-level timeline for ISO 27001 assessment (expected audit window and go/no-go gating milestones).
- FedRAMP readiness posture: whether you plan to pursue JAB/Agency authorization or a sponsor-led ATO, and an estimated intake window.
- Control ownership map for the control families Brightline will assess (information on who owns each control and an evidence contact).
- A sample list of artifacts we can expect to receive (logs, config snapshots, KMS attestation, SOC 2 bridge letters, SIG/CAIQ responses).

We are not asking for full evidence yet — just a ramp-check to set our auditor calendar. If you have a short spreadsheet or diagram you can share that maps controls -> owners -> tentative delivery weeks, that would be ideal.

Thanks,

Sarah Lewis
Security Operations Manager
Brightline Financial

[Attachment: none]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@brightline.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: roadmap, control owners & evidence windows for ISO/FedRAMP readiness

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick update from our side:

- ISO 27001: target certification audit window Q4 2027 (formal readiness review targeted for 2027-10-01). We expect the external auditor dry-run in late Sep.
- FedRAMP: pursuing sponsor-led ATO first (working with an agency partner). Intake planning session with the partner is scheduled for 2027-07-05; conservative readiness window would be H1 2028 for formal assessment.

Attached is an initial evidence matrix (draft) that maps high-level control families to tentative owners and what we anticipate delivering during the intake sprint. This is still a draft; owners listed are subject to confirmation.

Action items for our side:
- Olga: confirm owners for the infra/networking controls and provide expected artifact types + earliest snapshot dates.
- Kimberly: confirm application-level controls (access, RBAC, data classification) and any dependencies on 3p services.
- Marissa: legal/procurement will confirm contract-level attestations (SOC 2 bridge, vendor attestations).

We can do a short 30-min sync with your auditor next week if that helps finalize the calendar.

Thanks,

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Cloud Security (Redwood Inference)
[Attachment: Evidence_Matrix_v0.3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@brightline.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: roadmap, control owners & evidence windows for ISO/FedRAMP readiness

Folks —

I reviewed the draft matrix and added comments to the networking controls tab. Quick clarifications / notes:

- Network/infra evidence: we can provide VPC peering diagrams, NAT/bastion access logs, and a 7-day config snapshot for firewall rules. Earliest snapshot availability: 2027-06-25.
- KMS attestation: our KMS provider supports key rotation logs export; I will include the rotation audit extract sample.
- Sampling: for the FedRAMP intake we should expect the auditors to request 30-day rolling logs and a 1-week snapshot for config drift — I flagged those as "on-request" in the sheet.

Open question for Brightline: do you require proofs for our autoscaling transient instances (spot preemption logs) or are you focused on persistent worker fleets? That affects what we sample.

Attaching a small scope diagram to show which components are in-scope for ISO vs. FedRAMP (note: FedRAMP will likely include the control plane elements we purposefully isolate for agency tenants).

Olga
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Scope_Diagram_ISO_FedRAMP.png (image/png)]

From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@brightline.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, security@brightline.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: roadmap, control owners & evidence windows for ISO/FedRAMP readiness

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying replies from our audit lead: 

- For FedRAMP intake, auditors will want evidence showing the boundary includes both control plane and data plane for agency tenants. The snapshot cadence you suggested (7-day config + 30-day logs) is fine.
- Regarding transient instances: please include spot preemption logs if they can impact data residency or key handling workflows; otherwise call that out in the evidence narrative.
- We will take a look at the matrix and scope diagram and confirm next steps. Please mark any items in the matrix that are "delivery-by-request" vs. "standard delivery" so our intake team knows what needs a special pull.

Can we tentatively schedule a 30-min call on 2027-06-22 at 10:00am PT to review the matrix and confirm owners?

Best,

Sarah Lewis
Security Operations Manager
Brightline Financial
